verses.english: Linked Discourses 3.13
2. Childless
A Bucketful of Rice
At Sāvatthī.

verses.pali: Tena kho pana samayena rājā pasenadi kosalo doṇapākakuraṁ bhuñjati.
verses.english: Now at that time King Pasenadi of Kosala used to eat boiled rice by the bucketful.

verses.pali: Atha kho rājā pasenadi kosalo bhuttāvī mahassāsī yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi.
verses.english: Then after eating King Pasenadi of Kosala went up to the Buddha, huffing and puffing. He bowed and sat down to one side.

verses.pali: Atha kho bhagavā rājānaṁ pasenadiṁ kosalaṁ bhuttāviṁ mahassāsiṁ viditvā tāyaṁ velāyaṁ imaṁ gāthaṁ abhāsi:
verses.english: Then, knowing that King Pasenadi was huffing and puffing after eating, on that occasion the Buddha spoke this verse:
“When a man is always mindful,
knowing moderation in eating,
his discomfort fades,
and he ages slowly, taking care of his life.”

verses.pali: Tena kho pana samayena sudassano māṇavo rañño pasenadissa kosalassa piṭṭhito ṭhito hoti.
verses.english: Now at that time the student Sudassana was standing behind the king.

verses.pali: Atha kho rājā pasenadi kosalo sudassanaṁ māṇavaṁ āmantesi:
verses.english: Then King Pasenadi addressed him,

verses.pali: “ehi tvaṁ, tāta sudassana, bhagavato santike imaṁ gāthaṁ pariyāpuṇitvā mama bhattābhihāre bhattābhihāre bhāsa.
verses.english: “Please, dear Sudassana, memorize this verse in the Buddha’s presence and recite it to me whenever I am served a meal.

verses.pali: Ahañca te devasikaṁ kahāpaṇasataṁ kahāpaṇasataṁ niccaṁ bhikkhaṁ pavattayissāmī”ti.
verses.english: I’ll set up a regular daily allowance of a hundred dollars for you.”

verses.pali: “Evaṁ, devā”ti kho sudassano māṇavo rañño pasenadissa kosalassa paṭissutvā bhagavato santike imaṁ gāthaṁ pariyāpuṇitvā rañño pasenadissa kosalassa bhattābhihāre sudaṁ bhāsati:
verses.english: “Yes, Your Majesty,” replied Sudassana. He memorized that verse in the Buddha’s presence, and then whenever the king was served a meal he would repeat it:
“When a man is always mindful,
knowing moderation in eating,
his discomfort fades,
and he ages slowly, taking care of his life.”

verses.pali: Atha kho rājā pasenadi kosalo anupubbena nāḷikodanaparamatāya saṇṭhāsi.
verses.english: Then the king gradually got used to having at most a cup of rice.

verses.pali: Atha kho rājā pasenadi kosalo aparena samayena susallikhitagatto pāṇinā gattāni anumajjanto tāyaṁ velāyaṁ imaṁ udānaṁ udānesi:
verses.english: After some time King Pasenadi’s body slimmed right down. Stroking his limbs with his hands, at that time he expressed this heartfelt sentiment:

verses.pali: “ubhayena vata maṁ so bhagavā atthena anukampi—
verses.english: “In both ways the Buddha has sympathy for me:
in the good of this life and the good of the next.”
